title: Two measured dip depths give a thermal flux floor in an isothermal absorption model for TIC 300651846
abstract: We connect two simultaneous dip depths of TIC 300651846 to its possible thermal emission. A radiative equilibrium model uses the same effective absorption cross section for extinction, heating and emission. Positive mixtures allow any column distribution and extra visible material outside the stellar disk. Thermal light is included in the dip reference flux. For absorption index one and radius 2.49 stellar radii, the sampled minimum flux at 4.6028 micrometers is 0.526% of the bare-star flux. A joint Gaussian marginal-error rectangle gives a continuous-column numerical minimum bracket of 0.425% to 0.473%. A separate analytic inequality gives a weaker 0.296% floor without column sampling. Radius four and other opacity indices change the prediction. Independent quadrature and finer grids check the calculation. This is a conditional individual-star prediction, not a dust detection or an application of a population infrared limit. Isothermal isotropic elements, no scattering or mutual shielding, a blackbody star, nominal wavelengths and one selected dip limit the result. Original code, aggregate evidence, provenance and repeat instructions are included.

display.caption: Minimum thermal flux in a column-mixture model. Curves show feasible sampled minima at each wavelength separately. Dashed curves allow a joint depth-error rectangle. These are conditional predictions, not observed excesses. Continuous-column brackets are in the text and numerical files.
